body:

author: sidharthv96

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
I wouldn't recommend using magic numbers; if it were the default value, then it should be someplace similar to a `pie` diagram.
This also apply to this line:

<https://github.com/mermaid-js/mermaid/blob/d21461fba03dcd01ec82d7b152b2bb1ac786d4b4/packages/mermaid/src/diagrams/mindmap/mindmapDb.ts#L49>

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: Actually, now with the new type, we won't need the 10.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Recommends against magic numbers and suggests moving default values to a location similar to the pie diagram.

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body: Since it would be thrown right away, is there a reason to declare a variable for it?

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: I'm guessing it was for debugging maybe. No need to keep it.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Implies the variable declaration should be removed and the error thrown inline.

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body: I'm not sure if, if I understand this correctly, getting the current configurations would be equivalent to getting the default values.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body: Yes, but it's not typed. So this one marks all the values as required, so that we can access the props without `!` or `?` checks.

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
I see what it does mean, but I have two points:

1. Does it actually have all values defined? Does it handle the case when the user set an attribute as `undefined`? 
2. Using the `WithDefaults` part kind of shows it similar to `DEFAULT_CONFIG`, but it’s returning the current configuration, with the values having been overridden by the user. It's a kind of misleading name.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Flags a potential correctness issue with using current config vs. default values.

comments.author: Yokozuna59
comments.body:
Is there no other option for this approach? I'm not against it, but it would be better if we had some support from the developers themselves.

I think we could also use approach in #4880.

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
Yes, I'll raise a PR in cytoscape for native support. 

I didn't understand how the approach in #4880 would be useful here 🤔 Or did you mean using this approach in #4880?

comments.body:

I'm not sure, but shouldn't use the `Group` element itself instead of the `SVG` element:

```typescript
import type { DrawDefinition, Group, SVG } from '../../diagram-api/types.js';
```

```suggestion
  const group: Group = svg.append('g');
```

comments.body: I've removed that svg.append. The other g is coming from `appendDivSvgG`, removing without would be out of scope for this PR. I don't think there is a need for a parent Existing Updated

comments.author: sidharthv96
comments.body:
> Does it actually have all values defined? 

It _might_ not. But the type of defaultConfig is `RequiredDeep<MermaidConfig>`, so we're assuming it has all the values. 

> Does it handle the case when the user set an attribute as undefined?

No, runtime changes are not handled. 


Actually, I've removed that type now. We can reintroduce after some discussion in a separate PR.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Provides a direct code suggestion to use conf.mindmap.maxNodeWidth instead of a magic number.
